method.text: Every page read in ascending physical-page order using pypdf default extraction, with passages reread in the page image as needed. All 104 physical pages, including boundary page 308, were actually read.
method.visual: Every physical page 308-411 individually opened with view_image at 900 x 1350, rendered directly from the reading PDF by Ghostscript at 150 dpi. No contact-sheet or file-existence substitution. Pages 408-411 were reopened after an output truncation before attesting to their review.
method.image_numbering: Preview sequence 001 maps to reading-PDF physical page 308; physical page = sequence + 307.
method.coverage_limit: Editorial and visual review of the reading PDF only. Not an independent recertification of all historical, technical, legal or financial claims; specific pending verification is labeled. Illustration rights and external reference destinations were not independently audited. No manuscript or PDF edits made.

findings.reason: Elijah presents the cost per meal and funding date, then skips to the last slide on page 324. Fourteen slides cannot all remain unshown on page 326.
findings.suggested_correction: Replace with "most of his slides unshown" or "the unused slides". This preserves the emotional beat without changing the scene.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.quote: Have them while people are being fed, not as a condition for starting.
findings.reason: This can be read as authorizing a service before its funding is secured, contrary to the bounded, funded promise carefully established in Chapter 18 and the scene. The urgency can remain while distinguishing a funded pilot from continuing provision.
findings.suggested_correction: Consider: "Start with provision you can fund now. Keep people fed while you negotiate the continuing commitment."
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.quote: We aren’t “destroying jobs”; we’re automating the toil and the risk
findings.reason: The same page acknowledges people whose paid work goes away, and the preceding conclusion takes their loss seriously. Quotation marks do not resolve the denial of actual job loss.
findings.suggested_correction: Consider: "Jobs can disappear. Automating toil and risk doesn’t relieve us of responsibility to the people who did them." Preserve the insistence that benefits reach those people.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.quote: That voice is the last fence, and it’s the only one nobody else can tear down for you.
findings.reason: Calling self-doubt the last barrier discounts the funding, time, disability, care and institutional barriers the book otherwise recognizes. Saying nobody else can help also conflicts with its strongest examples of learning together.
findings.suggested_correction: Consider: "That voice is one fence you can start taking down, with someone beside you." Keep the invitation and remove the implication that access rests on attitude alone.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.reason: Inline source titles lack grammatical and typographic separation from surrounding print prose. This is visible in the page images, not merely an extraction artifact. It interrupts otherwise careful argument and reference boundaries.
findings.suggested_correction: Render source labels consistently as parenthetical references or endnotes, with appropriate sentence punctuation and preserved link destinations. Review every affected page after reflow.
findings.verification: confirmed visually; source-link destination correctness was not audited

findings.quote: what comes in (calories, kilowatt-hours, dollars), what goes out (labor, attention, rent), and who captures the spread.
findings.reason: Appendix G retains older wording that invites arithmetic across unlike quantities. Chapter 5 now says who gets paid and explicitly requires keeping each quantity in its own units, so the checklist does not preserve the revised exercise.
findings.suggested_correction: Synchronize with Chapter 5: "Run the energy audit on paper: what comes in, what goes out, and who gets paid. Keep calories, kilowatt-hours, dollars, and hours in their own units."
findings.verification: confirmed against src/lib/data/book/07-chapter5.md:199 as well as the appendix page

findings.reason: Month 1 items 3 and 4 ask for substantially overlapping files of AI predictions with claim, date and author. Two containers add work without explaining a useful distinction.
findings.suggested_correction: Combine into one predictions file containing the claim, author, publication date, stated forecast date and later outcome. Keep both P-03 and P-24 references if they serve different review habits.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.quote: Ask someone at least fifteen years younger than you who uses AI daily
findings.reason: Chapter 18 explicitly includes readers under twenty-five. For a twenty-year-old, this instruction requires a child aged five or younger, making an otherwise useful exercise inaccessible to part of the named audience.
findings.suggested_correction: Use "Ask someone who uses AI differently from you" or provide an age-neutral alternative while retaining the twenty-minute observation and first-ten-minutes listening instructions.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.quote: Several famous technology quotes are fabrications
findings.reason: The paragraph moves from failed primary-source verification to categorical fabrication, then claims an example is the most cited online and that no archival record has ever been produced. Those are broader claims than the bibliography establishes. This finding does not assert that the disputed quotations are authentic.
findings.suggested_correction: Use bounded sourcing language: "I left out several familiar technology quotations because I couldn’t verify them in reliable primary sources." Remove the unmeasured most-cited claim and absolute archival assertion, or attach documented provenance supporting each one.
findings.verification: source verification pending; certainty and missing-support issue confirmed by internal reading only

findings.quote: starts a loop that runs faster each turn
findings.reason: The glossary makes acceleration sound mechanically assured, while the Good bibliography entry explicitly describes a conditional prospect rather than a demonstrated sequence of unlimited improvement. A reference definition should retain that distinction.
findings.suggested_correction: Consider: "I. J. Good’s 1965 idea: a machine able to design better machines could start a reinforcing loop of further improvements. Its pace and limits remain open questions."
findings.verification: confirmed internal comparison; no independent claim about empirical limits is added

findings.quote: After food, the order is land care, cleanup, shelter, then everything further out.
findings.reason: Chapter 18 puts shelter and care next; Chapter 19 gives food, shelter, care, transport and information. Appendix C and the glossary instead put land care and cleanup before shelter. These may describe different planning scales, but the summaries call both the book’s priority order.
findings.suggested_correction: Clarify whether one sequence concerns practical project priorities and the other expanding public services. If that distinction is intended, label it explicitly in both summaries. Otherwise use the author-confirmed order consistently; do not silently select a policy priority.
findings.verification: confirmed by direct text reading and full-page visual inspection

findings.reason: The symptom index returns only a P-number, while the main ledger returns chapter numbers. The promised rapid print lookup requires several searches before a reader reaches the passage.
findings.suggested_correction: Add generated printed-page locators to the ledger and symptom index, together with active PDF/EPUB links to stable precedent anchors. Generate these from the final layout so revision cannot stale them.
findings.verification: print-retrieval limitation confirmed visually; existing PDF annotation destinations were not independently inspected

findings.quote: Go back through this list and pick the one that made you most uncomfortable.
findings.reason: Month 12’s final numbered action and two closing lines occupy a separate page with most of its body empty. This looks like an accidental spill and separates the annual review from its conclusion.
findings.suggested_correction: Rebalance Appendix G so Month 12 and its closing paragraph remain together, using suitable list spacing or an earlier safe break. Preserve body-text size and review the resulting adjacent pages.
findings.verification: confirmed by full-page visual inspection; precise pagination cause not yet established

verified_questions.question: Does the return scene falsely imply permanent funding after the county vote?
verified_questions.result: No. June becomes December in the vote, and funding beyond December remains unresolved in the return scene. Preserve the partial victory.

verified_questions.question: Does the mother’s call introduce a chronology inconsistency?
verified_questions.result: No. The scene explicitly locates the call four days earlier; retain that temporal cue.

verified_questions.question: Do fused words in extracted epigraph-source text necessarily indicate missing visual spaces?
verified_questions.result: No. Direct page inspection shows separation in several extracted runs. Only visually confirmed source-title collisions are reported.

verified_questions.question: Is the repeated Israel Batch 3 URL a duplicated credit?
verified_questions.result: No. The source page also supplies the stated public-domain dedication. Repetition here is not itself a defect.

strengths: The county-board scene and the final bar scene earn a partial victory through specific people, paid work, dates and unresolved obligations.
The strongest policy pages distinguish capacity from access and keep units, reporting periods, institutional scope and maintenance visible.
The source apparatus usually distinguishes primary documents, company histories, later interpretation and forecast, which makes the remaining overcertainty easy to correct locally.
Cyberdeck tiers and the first-year structure give readers ways to begin at modest scale. Most tables, figures, captions and source pages are readable with no observed clipping.

mechanical_validation.limit: These checks establish record completeness and byte binding. They cannot establish that an editor read or understood a page; that attestation is supplied only after the recorded direct review.
